title: Keep a nonlinear boundary transient outside initial-state/equilibrium shortcuts
statement: In 2A+B<->3A with unit constants, c=(1,1), w=(1,1), n=1,V>=4,x0=(2,V-2),T=V, the ACTUAL class is2<=A<=V. Initial exit rate is2(V-2)/V^2; no-event mass tends e^-2, while stationary pi(A=2)=binom(V,2)/(2^V-V-1) tends0. Thus liminf endpoint-to-equilibrium TV>=e^-2. First jump beforeV/2 and no further jump gives liminf P(A(V)=3)>=(1-e^-1)e^-6, excluding return-x0 at arbitrarily small error. The exact stationary reverse has kappa*=kappa*c^y/c^z and unchanged symmetric diffusion, with P_T(x0,x)=pi(x)/pi(x0)*P_T^*(x,x0); this mature adjoint identity does not supply a bridge sampler. Any corresponding stationary-proposal rejection envelope obeys M>=exp(-2(V-2)/V)*(2^V-V-1)/binom(V,2)=Omega(2^V/V^2), a strategy-specific failure. Root also gives j=A-2,N=V-2: birth/death rates (j+1)(j+2)(N-j)/V^2 and (j+1)(j+2)j/V^2, so L_X=g(j)L_Ehrenfest/V^2; physical clock integral V^2/[(Y+1)(Y+2)] is trajectory-dependent. Efficient joint clock-functional sampling is OPEN. These are not a universal impossibility theorem.
